title: Consonants
description: Polish consonant sounds that do not exist, or are easy to mispronounce, in English.

items.description: Voiceless retroflex fricative, spelled sz. Similar to the English "sh", but the tongue tip curls further back.
Voiceless retroflex affricate, spelled cz: a short "t" released into the sz sound above.
Voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate, spelled ć (or ci before a vowel). Softer and further forward than cz; the two are a common source of confusion for learners.
items.note: Contrasts with cz /t͡ʂ/: czy ("whether") vs. ci ("you", informal dative).

items.description: Voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative, spelled ś (or si before a vowel). Softer than sz, produced with the tongue body raised toward the hard palate.
Voiced labio-velar approximant, spelled ł. Pronounced like the English "w" in "water" — not like an English "l" at all, which trips up most beginners.
Palatal nasal, spelled ń (or ni before a vowel). Close to the Spanish ñ in "señor".
